meta.purpose: Starting library of hypotheses, verification checks, corrective actions and improvement ideas per SEU type. Items are HYPOTHESES to verify on site (ISO 50002-style measurement/inspection), not diagnoses. Edit and extend with your plant's own history (past audit findings, MOCs, maintenance records).
meta.how_used: The notebook picks entries by seu_type + detected deviation pattern (drift | step | spike | persistent_high) and by improvement triggers (high_baseload | weather_sensitive | bdp_gap | always).

likely_causes: Progressive fouling, wear or loss of efficiency of the equipment
Control setpoints creeping or valves left partly open/bypassed
Instrument drift or changed operating practice
verify: Compare current operating point against design/test data at equal load
Review maintenance and operating logs since the drift started
Check calibration of the energy and process meters
corrective: Inspect and clean/restore the equipment at the next opportunity
Restore setpoints and valve line-ups to the reference
Add the SEU's deviation trend to the monthly review

likely_causes: Change in equipment line-up, setpoint, product/grade or operating mode
Equipment fault or bypass started at the step date
Change in metering or data source
verify: Identify what changed on the step date (MOC, shift log, maintenance order)
Confirm the meter and data source did not change
corrective: Reverse the change if it was unintended
If intended, document its energy impact and re-assess the baseline per procedure

likely_causes: One-off operating event (start-up, trial, upset, flushing)
Temporary extra equipment running
verify: Check the events log and shift reports for the spike month
corrective: Record the cause in the events log; no equipment action unless it repeats

high_baseload: A large share of this energy does not depend on production: identify idle/standby running and turndown options (ISO 50002 audit measurement at low load)
weather_sensitive: Energy depends on ambient temperature: review setpoints, heat-rejection performance and cleaning schedule
bdp_gap: Best demonstrated performance is better than typical: study what operating practice was used in the best months and standardize it
always: Install or confirm sub-metering with a monthly data check
Set an alarm limit on the deviation so drift is caught early

likely_causes: Impeller wear or increased internal clearance lowering efficiency
Strainer, filter or line fouling raising differential pressure (slurry service: polymer/solids build-up)
Control valves throttling more over time, or recycle/minimum-flow line passing
verify: Trend motor current/power at constant flow and compare with the pump curve
Check strainer/filter differential pressure and line fouling indicators
Check recycle/spillback valve positions and leakage
corrective: Clean strainers/filters; schedule loop or line cleaning if fouling is confirmed
Overhaul pump or restore clearances/impeller if worn
Reopen throttled valves and fix recycle leakage

likely_causes: Additional pump started or standby pump left running in parallel
Changed operating point (new grade, density, flow target)
VSD bypassed or fixed at higher speed
verify: Check pump line-up and running hours per pump
Confirm VSD status and speed setpoint
Compare flow and head with the pre-step period
corrective: Stop the unneeded pump or restore the intended line-up
Restore VSD control and speed setpoint

likely_causes: Start-up, flushing or cleaning operation
Temporary parallel running during maintenance
verify: Check events log and operating log for that month
corrective: Log the cause; no equipment action unless it repeats

high_baseload: Match pump duty to actual demand: trim impeller or fit VSD where flow is regularly throttled
Review whether a smaller pump or on/off staging can serve low-load periods
weather_sensitive: Review fluid temperature/viscosity effects on pumping power
bdp_gap: Standardize the line-up and valve positions used during the best-performing months
always: Track pump efficiency against best efficiency point (BEP) at the usual operating point

likely_causes: Intercooler/aftercooler fouling raising gas temperature and power
Suction filter or line pressure drop increasing
Anti-surge/recycle valve passing or partly open
Valve or seal wear (reciprocating) / internal leakage
Higher discharge pressure setpoint or downstream pressure drop
verify: Trend compression ratio, interstage and discharge temperatures
Check anti-surge/recycle valve position and recycle flow at steady load
Compute polytropic (or isentropic) efficiency trend
Check suction filter differential pressure
corrective: Clean coolers/exchangers; schedule cleaning by measured approach temperature
Repair or re-stroke the recycle/anti-surge valve; tighten the anti-surge margin if safe
Overhaul valves/seals as indicated
Restore pressure setpoints

likely_causes: Anti-surge or recycle valve opened or failed open
Changed discharge pressure target or process line-up
Standby unit running with duty unit
verify: Check recycle flow, valve positions and unit line-up on the step date
Confirm setpoint history in the control system
corrective: Close or repair the recycle path
Restore discharge pressure target and unit line-up

likely_causes: Start-up/restart, upset or heavy recycle during a disturbance
verify: Check events log and trip/restart history
corrective: Log the cause; review start-up practice if it repeats

high_baseload: Reduce recycle at low throughput (turndown strategy); review compressor loading steps or speed control
weather_sensitive: Improve cooling of suction/interstage gas: keep coolers clean and cooling water at design temperature
bdp_gap: Study operating conditions (pressure ratio, recycle) in the best months and set them as targets
always: Add online efficiency monitoring (polytropic efficiency vs load)

likely_causes: Screw/barrel wear reducing efficiency
Screen pack or die plugging raising pressure and power
Gearbox or lubrication losses
verify: Compare specific energy (kWh or GJ per ton) by grade at equal throughput
Trend screen pack differential pressure and melt temperature
Check gearbox oil condition and temperature
corrective: Change screens on a measured differential-pressure limit
Inspect screw/barrel clearances at the next shutdown
Service gearbox and lubrication

likely_causes: Different product slate (higher viscosity grades)
Reduced throughput (fixed losses spread over fewer tons)
Equipment change (screw/die refurbishment) - may be an improvement
verify: Compare specific energy by grade before/after the step
Check the events log for equipment changes and trials
corrective: Set grade-specific energy targets and operating windows
If the step is downward after an equipment change, confirm and consider re-baselining per procedure

likely_causes: Grade trial or off-spec run with frequent screen changes
Restart after a trip/plant outage
verify: Check the events log and production log for that month
corrective: Record the trial energy cost; schedule trials with planned start-ups

high_baseload: Run at higher throughput and minimize idle/low-rate running; plan campaigns by grade
weather_sensitive: Review barrel/gearbox cooling for ambient sensitivity
bdp_gap: Define best-practice setpoints (temperature profile, screw speed) from the best months, per grade
always: Report specific energy by grade; evaluate high-efficiency motors/drives at next replacement

likely_causes: Steam trap failures or condensate return degradation
Insulation damage and heat losses
Rising purge gas/nitrogen flow or heater fouling
verify: Run a steam trap survey (ultrasonic/thermographic)
Check condensate return flow and temperature
Compare steam per ton of product against the baseline
corrective: Repair or replace failed traps; restore insulation
Restore condensate return
Clean heater surfaces and tune purge flow

likely_causes: Blowing steam trap or leak that started at the step date
Higher dryer temperature/steam pressure setpoint
Higher inlet moisture or product change
Condensate return line lost
verify: Check what changed on the step date (setpoints, maintenance orders)
Steam trap survey and condensate return check
Check inlet moisture and product slate
corrective: Repair the leak/trap or restore setpoints
Restore the condensate return line
Tune dryer temperature to the moisture specification instead of a fixed margin

likely_causes: Start-up, off-spec reprocessing or abnormal wet product
verify: Check events log and quality records for that month
corrective: Log the cause; review start-up steam use

high_baseload: Reduce idle steam and purge flow at low throughput; review start-up/stand-by steam use
weather_sensitive: Review insulation and heat loss at ambient conditions
bdp_gap: Replicate the best months' dryer temperature and purge setpoints
always: Install a steam trap management program with a scheduled survey
Consider heat recovery from dryer vent

cooling.label: Cooling water pumps and tower fans

likely_causes: Fouled heat exchangers raising required flow
Cooling tower fill/nozzle fouling raising approach temperature
Fans/pumps running at full speed regardless of load
verify: Check cooling water supply/return temperature difference and tower approach
Check fan and pump staging/speed and control mode
Check exchanger approach temperatures
corrective: Clean tower fill, nozzles and key exchangers
Set fan/pump staging to load and ambient
Fix control loops holding fans at high speed

likely_causes: Extra pump or fan started or control mode changed
Higher heat load from a process change
verify: Check pump/fan line-up and control mode history
Compare process heat load before and after
corrective: Restore staging and automatic control

likely_causes: Temporary full-flow operation during maintenance or upset
verify: Check events log
corrective: Log the cause

high_baseload: Reduce flow where return temperature is below design (low delta-T)
weather_sensitive: Optimize fan staging against wet-bulb temperature; maintain tower approach
bdp_gap: Replicate fan/pump control settings from the best months
always: Evaluate VSDs on fans and pumps; track delta-T and approach monthly

likely_causes: Growing leakage
Pressure setpoint raised to compensate for demand or drops
Filter/dryer pressure drop increasing
Poor compressor sequencing with unloaded running
verify: Ultrasonic leak survey; estimate leakage at no-load demand
Check header pressure and pressure drop across filters and dryers
Check unloaded run hours and specific power (kW per m3/min)
corrective: Repair leaks and keep a leak tag log
Lower the header pressure to the minimum acceptable
Replace or clean filters and fix dryers
Optimize sequencing with a master controller

likely_causes: A new consumer or open blow-off/drain
An additional compressor running or sequencing changed
Pressure setpoint raised
verify: Check compressor loading/unloading hours and line-up
Walk the system for open blow-offs
corrective: Close inappropriate uses; restore sequencing and setpoints

likely_causes: Maintenance purge, cleaning or test activity
verify: Check events log
corrective: Log the cause

high_baseload: Find and fix leaks (often the largest base load); shut down compressors at no demand
Reduce pressure to the minimum needed
weather_sensitive: Review intake air temperature and compressor room ventilation
bdp_gap: Replicate the best months' sequencing and pressure setpoints
always: Add a VSD trim compressor where load fluctuates; review heat recovery

likely_causes: Combustion efficiency decline: excess oxygen too high or burner out of tune
Fouled heat-transfer surfaces (fireside or waterside) raising stack temperature
Excessive blowdown or lower condensate return
Steam leaks or failed traps in distribution
verify: Check flue gas O2/CO and stack temperature trend
Check blowdown rate vs conductivity limit and condensate return fraction
Check steam trap and leak survey results
corrective: Tune burner and O2 trim; clean heat-transfer surfaces
Optimize blowdown; restore condensate return
Repair steam leaks and failed traps

likely_causes: Boiler line-up change (additional boiler at low load)
Burner/controls change or manual mode
Condensate return lost
verify: Check which boilers ran and at what load
Check O2 trim and burner control mode
corrective: Restore boiler loading strategy and controls

likely_causes: Start-up, boil-out or hot standby
verify: Check events log
corrective: Log the cause

high_baseload: Review hot standby and low-load boiler operation; consolidate load on fewer boilers
bdp_gap: Replicate the best months' O2 target and boiler loading
always: Evaluate economizer and blowdown heat recovery, O2 trim, and condensate return improvement

likely_causes: Condenser fouling or high condenser water temperature
Low chilled-water delta-T with poor staging
Refrigerant charge or non-condensable issues
verify: Trend kW per ton of refrigeration vs load
Check approach temperatures and delta-T
Check staging logic and part-load operation
corrective: Clean condenser tubes; restore condenser water temperature control
Optimize chiller staging
Check refrigerant charge and purge

likely_causes: Lower chilled-water setpoint or extra chiller running
Higher load from a process change
verify: Check setpoint and staging history
corrective: Restore setpoint and staging

likely_causes: Start-up or temporary high load
verify: Check events log
corrective: Log the cause

high_baseload: Review minimum load operation and staging at low demand
weather_sensitive: Optimize condenser water temperature reset; evaluate free cooling where possible
bdp_gap: Replicate the best months' setpoints and staging
always: Evaluate chilled-water temperature reset and VSD chillers/pumps

likely_causes: Schedule or setpoint drift
Simultaneous heating and cooling or reheat
Dirty filters/coils reducing efficiency
Lighting left on outside working hours
verify: Check BMS schedules and setpoints
Check filters and coils
Night-time walk-through for lighting and equipment left on
corrective: Restore schedules and setpoints
Clean filters and coils
Add occupancy/time controls

likely_causes: Schedule or setpoint change
New area or equipment added
verify: Check BMS change log
corrective: Restore schedule/setpoints or document the new load

likely_causes: Event, commissioning or temporary conditions
verify: Check events log
corrective: Log the cause

high_baseload: Reduce out-of-hours load with schedules and occupancy controls
weather_sensitive: Optimize cooling setpoints; improve envelope/solar control
bdp_gap: Replicate the best months' schedules and setpoints
always: LED lighting with controls; BMS optimization

likely_causes: Burner out of tune or high excess air
Door/seal leakage and insulation losses
Higher exhaust temperature or reduced hot-air recirculation
Rising moisture load in the product
verify: Check exhaust O2 and temperature
Check seals, insulation and air balance
Compare energy per kg of water removed
corrective: Tune burner and excess air
Repair seals and insulation
Restore recirculation and air balance

likely_causes: Temperature setpoint raised or product change
Recirculation damper or burner control change
verify: Check setpoint history and recent maintenance
corrective: Restore setpoints and damper positions

likely_causes: Start-up or product changeover
verify: Check events log
corrective: Log the cause

high_baseload: Reduce idle heating between batches or lines; improve start-up scheduling
weather_sensitive: Review insulation and intake air conditions
bdp_gap: Replicate the best months' temperature and air settings
always: Evaluate exhaust heat recovery and moisture-based control of drying

verdict_notes.activity_driven: Energy per ton is higher, but total energy follows the baseline model for the actual production and weather. This is mostly a load effect (fixed energy spread over fewer tons), not equipment deterioration. Do not chase equipment faults; look at reducing fixed/base load at low throughput and at production scheduling.
verdict_notes.improvement: Energy is persistently below the baseline model. Confirm the cause (equipment change, practice change, or meter/data issue), document it, and consider re-baselining only through the controlled procedure.
verdict_notes.normal: Within the deviation band. Keep monitoring.
